title: Tübingen PET Intervention Register
summary:
The subject of the intervention registry is PET/CT or PET/MRI, combinations of positron emission tomography (PET) and computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). These are diagnostic imaging techniquse that allow the simultaneous visualization of structure and function of tissues in (three-dimensional) slices. 

In the registry, pseudonymized (=encoded) data of patients who have received a PET/CT or PET/MRI examination are recorded. The groups of patients included in the registry can have very different diseases. 

The aim of the registry is to collect information on PET/CT ans PET/MRI examinations from as many patients as possible in a database and to evaluate it under different aspects. This data from everyday clinical practice will help to ensure the quality of hybrid imaging. For this purpose, for example, it will be recorded why a PET/CT or PET/MRI examination was performed in the first place and whether or how the diagnosis helped to plan further treatment. The collected data will help to develop guidelines that can support the decision making of physicians and patients to undergo hybrid imaging examinations. For a better evaluation of the cost-benefit ratio of PET/CT and PET/MRI examinations, this form of quality assurance is also demanded by some service providers ("health insurance companies").

Thus, the PET registry in Tübingen serves to promote medical quality and health care research.
conditions: Diverse, patients with clinical indication for PET/CT or PET/MRI examination

interventions.name:
Patients for whom a PET/CT or PET/MRI examination is performed due to a clinical indication.
Patients receive PET/CT or PET/MRI as part of routine clinical practice. Data on the performance of PET/CT or PET/MRI and on the clinical findings and disease status are entered into a register.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients for whom a PET/CT or PET/MRI examination has been requested and will be performed at the Department of Radiology of the University Hospital Tuebingen due to a clinical indication.
- Written informed consent of the patient or the patient's legal guardian.
Exclusion criteria:
- no patient consent or consent of the legal guardian for data collection in the Tübingen PET registry
